Definition: to push, gore, defeat, stub (the toe), inflict (a disease)
BiblicalUsage: Nagaph means to smite or strike, to push against and bring down, and it is used for the Passover, for plague, and for stumbling. In Exodus 12:23 the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians, but will not suffer the destroyer to come into the houses with the blood on the door, and in 2 Chronicles 21:18 the Lord smote Jehoram in his bowels with an incurable disease. In 1 Samuel 7:10 the Lord thunders with a great thunder on the Philistines and discomfits them, and in 1 Samuel 25:38 the Lord smites Nabal about ten days after, and he dies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the smiting in this word always has a purpose, whether it is judgment on Egypt, disease on a wicked king, or the thunder that routs an army. The blood on the door in Exodus 12:23 is the difference between the smiting that passes over and the smiting that falls. I hold that the Lord who smites also shields, and the door marked with blood is the sign of it.
